findings.detail: `verify-evidence.mjs:145` excludes the whole bundle directory from the coverage check, with the correct reason: the bundle is generated *from* the review, so requiring it to be reviewed is circular. But `verify-attestation.mjs:148` (`SELF`) and `attest-review.mjs:130` (`EXCLUDED`) still exclude only `.apexyard/attestation`, its `.sig`, and `allowed_signers`. CI runs BOTH — step 6 uses the narrow exclusion and is a hard gate ahead of step 6b. Because `evidence.mjs` rewrites all seven artifacts whenever the attestation digest changes (and the digest covers `head`, which changes on every amend), there is no ordering that converges: on a first push the artifacts aren't in the attested scope, so committing them yields "changed in this range but were never reviewed"; on any later push they ARE attested, but at their pre-regeneration OIDs, so committing the refresh yields ".apexyard/review.json changed after it was reviewed". Amend-and-rerun reproduces the same state one commit along, forever. `attestation.json` mirrors the digest that covers it, so a fixed point cannot exist by construction. `test-evidence.sh:221` asserts exactly this requirement ("committing the bundle does not trip the coverage check") but only against the new verifier, which is why the gap shipped.
findings.summary: Committing the evidence bundle can never satisfy CI step 6; the gate has no fixed point

findings.detail: The manifest records `head 45b45fea…` (HEAD~1) and 22 files from the previous commit's range, while HEAD (88e2919) changed 28 files. Content binding fails on at least four attested paths — `.gitignore` attested `e94de656…`, now `8bd4a249…`; `package.json` `b591e359…` → `2a2526ce…`; `scripts/verify-local.sh` `c8078f01…` → `23710449…`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `d0de116d…` → `405d3585…` — and roughly a dozen files added by HEAD (`scripts/evidence.mjs`, `scripts/lib/{evidence,collectors}.mjs`, `scripts/verify-evidence.mjs`, `tests/unit/evidence.test.ts`, `eslint.config.js`, `docs/adr/ADR-0003…`) appear nowhere in it, so the coverage check fails too. Independently, line 8-9 record `verdict REQUEST_CHANGES` with `findings … high=1`, so `gateSatisfied(F, 'high')` returns "1 unresolved high finding(s)" regardless of the OIDs. Both CI steps 6 and 6b are hard gates feeding the required aggregate `CI` check, so this PR fails its own gate on every push. The mechanism is working as designed — it is the bundle that was not refreshed after the ADR-0003 work landed.
findings.summary: The committed attestation is stale against HEAD and records an unresolved high finding

findings.detail: `report()` is called at lines 94, 102 and 113 — missing attestation, malformed attestation, digest mismatch — but it reads `ID` (const, line 105), `F` (line 106), `headSha` (line 121) and `changed` (line 146), all of which are still in their temporal dead zone at those points. Every one of those three paths dies with `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'ID' before initialization` instead of emitting the `## Evidence bundle FAILED` report, the `::error` annotation, and the remediation block. The `typeof headSha === 'string'` guard at line 284 shows the intent was for `report()` to be callable early; `typeof` does not protect against TDZ (only against undeclared identifiers), so the guard is inert. Node exits 1 on the uncaught throw, so the gate still fails — but with a stack trace in place of the diagnostics, on exactly the paths a maintainer is most likely to hit.
findings.summary: Early report() calls throw ReferenceError instead of printing the failure report

findings.detail: `import('node:fs').then(({ appendFileSync }) => appendFileSync(...))` schedules a microtask, and `process.exit(1)` / `process.exit(0)` at lines 349 and 351 run synchronously immediately after, so the callback never executes. The `Evidence bundle` job therefore always emits `::error title=Evidence bundle::N problem(s) — see the job summary` pointing at a summary that is empty, and the success path contributes nothing either. `verify-attestation.mjs:286-289` gets this right with a top-level `await import(...)`, so this is a regression against the sibling verifier rather than a shared limitation.
findings.summary: The GitHub job summary is never written — process.exit() beats the async import

findings.detail: `.apexyard/review/review.json` is gitignored (`.gitignore:28`), but `evidence.mjs:100` is the only source for `review.json` and `findings.json`. Regenerate the bundle anywhere that file is absent — a second machine, a fresh clone, or after clearing `.apexyard/review/` — and both artifacts become `{available: false, reason: 'no review output at …'}`. Every cross-check that would notice is guarded on it: line 237 (`review?.available && findings?.available`) and line 255 (`review?.available && F.findings`) both short-circuit, `checkArtifact` only inspects canonicality/schema/id/determinism, and `missingArtifacts` only checks presence. So the bundle verifies clean while recording no review data at all — the same "never ran and passed look identical" failure the collectors were explicitly written to prevent, reintroduced one layer up at the verifier. The review gate itself is not bypassed (`gateSatisfied` still reads the manifest's counts), which is what keeps this at medium; it would be high if the manifest counts were sourced from `review.json`.
findings.summary: A bundle whose review.json says available:false passes verification

findings.detail: The bundle's central claim is byte-for-byte reproducibility from reviewed content, but two inputs come from the environment rather than from git. `directLicences` (line 127) reads `node_modules/*/package.json`, so the committed `dependency-report.json` records real licences on an installed tree and `{"unknown": 27}` without one. `collectArchitecture` (`collectors.mjs:344`, via `walkSources`) walks the filesystem, so an untracked scratch `.ts` file inflates `source_files`, `total_loc` and `by_directory` in a committed artifact that claims to describe the repository. Neither fails the gate today — stage 11's `--check` compares against what stage 10 just wrote, and CI never regenerates — so the effect is a silently environment-dependent artifact plus a misleading "a collector is not deterministic" message for anyone who runs `npm run evidence:check` on a fresh clone.
findings.summary: Two collectors read the working tree, so the bundle records state the repo does not contain

findings.detail: Git resolves attributes with last-matching-line-wins per attribute. `*  text=auto` on line 22 matches `.apexyard/attestation.sig` and re-sets `text`, overriding the deliberate `-text` on line 20 — so git is free to line-ending-normalise the one file the comment says it must not touch. An ssh-keygen armoured signature is detected as text, so on a `core.autocrlf=true` checkout the blob can come back CRLF and `ssh-keygen -Y verify` fails against a manifest that is correct. Latent today: no `attestation.sig` is committed and `allowed_signers` is absent, so nothing verifies signatures yet. It becomes a real verification failure the moment a key is registered (the TD-027 revisit trigger). The `eol=lf` lines above are unaffected — `eol` is a separate attribute that line 22 does not set.
findings.summary: Trailing `* text=auto` overrides the `-text` protecting the signature

findings.detail: `files_with_findings` maps every offending ESLint result through `toPosixRelative`, sorts the resulting array, and then discards all of it via `.length`. The path normalisation and the sort are dead work, and the field name reads like it holds the list — a later reader is likely to "fix" it by dropping the `.length` and silently put absolute developer paths into a committed artifact, which is exactly the non-reproducibility the module header warns about.
findings.summary: files_with_findings builds and sorts an array only to take its length

findings.detail: `(v as { impact?: string }).impact ?? null` casts away the declared type to read `impact`, which `Violation` (line 29) already declares as `impact?: string | null`. The cast is not narrowing anything — it silences nothing and hides the fact that the field is already typed, so a future change to `Violation` will not be type-checked at this line. The broader `results.violations as Violation[]` on line 93 is the load-bearing assertion; leaving the second, redundant one next to it makes the first look equally decorative.
findings.summary: Redundant inline cast to read a property the local type already declares
